title: The Geometry of Low-Resource Language Representations
abstract: arXiv:2608.23358v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The performance gap between low- and high-resource languages in LLMs is widely known, but it remains unclear which internal model factors drive these disparities. In this paper, we characterise this gap through the lens of representational geometry. Comparing the geometric properties of hidden representations across 30 languages reveals that LLM geometry is systematically related to language data availability. The most consistent effect is in final layers, where low-resource languages exhibit representational degeneration. To counter this, we investigate the effectiveness of regularisation terms to penalise degeneration during continued pretraining (CPT). Experiments monolingually adapting 9 base LLMs to 10 African languages show that geometric regularisation successfully reduces representational degeneration during CPT. translated_title: 低资源语言表征的几何特性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在低资源语言与高资源语言之间的性能差距广为人知，但驱动这些差异的内部模型因素仍不明确。本文通过表征几何的视角来刻画这一差距。比较30种语言隐藏表征的几何属性揭示出，LLM的几何结构与语言数据的可用性存在系统性关联。最一致的影响出现在最终层，其中低资源语言表现出表征退化现象。为应对这一问题，我们研究了在持续预训练（CPT）期间引入正则化项以惩罚退化的有效性。将9个基础LLM单语适配到10种非洲语言的实验表明，几何正则化能成功减少CPT期间的表征退化。对于较大模型，基于余弦相似度的正则化在性能上略优于普通CPT，且效果更佳。
tldr: 本文发现低资源语言在大型语言模型最终层存在表征退化，并提出几何正则化方法在持续预训练中有效缓解该问题，尤其对较大模型性能有轻微提升。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that low-resource languages exhibit representational degeneration in the final layers of LLMs, and proposes geometric regularization that effectively mitigates this during continued pretraining, with slight performance gains for larger models.
